references.text: The glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle, confirming that God consecrated the tent of meeting as He promised in 29:44
Moses anoints the tabernacle and the altar, and ordains Aaron for priestly service, fulfilling God's promise to consecrate them
The priest must be holy because the Lord who sanctifies him is holy - this elaborates on the consecration of Aaron and his sons
God commands that Aaron and his sons be anointed and ordained for His priestly service
The altar and the priests are to be anointed and consecrated for service to the Lord
The prophecy that God's sanctuary will be in the midst of the people forever, as an eschatological fulfillment of God's presence
The first covenant had a earthly tent and sanctuary, pointing forward to the perfect consecration in Christ
Believers are now a holy priesthood offering spiritual sacrifices, fulfilling the promise of sanctification
Believers are a royal priesthood and a holy nation, showing how God's sanctification now applies to all who believe
God's purpose to consecrate (29:44) is met by the specific instruction on how this is to be done (30:30).
40:13 shows the actual fulfillment of the consecration promised in 29:44.
29:21 describes the concrete ritual that realizes God's promise to consecrate in 29:44.
